title: Identity and Secrets
overview: This objective covers who and what authenticates to Claude: API keys and workspaces in the Console, Admin API keys, Console roles, key rotation, and how Claude Code picks among its many credential sources (API key, subscription OAuth, cloud provider, apiKeyHelper, long-lived OAuth tokens, gateways). It also covers keeping secrets out of reach: MCP OAuth and env expansion, deny rules for secret files, and gateway patterns. The exam tests precedence order, which key or role fits a scenario, and which control actually enforces a secret boundary.

sections.heading: API keys: types, headers, and the SDK environment variable
notes: API keys are static `sk-ant-api...` secrets created on the Console API keys page. Send them as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; the legacy `x-api-key` header is still supported.
The official SDKs read the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable automatically, so `Anthropic()` with no arguments works when it is set.

Key types: **personal key** (acts as you, with your roles), **service account key** (acts as a service account, for shared or automated workloads), and **workspace key** (legacy; belongs to the workspace, not a person).

Personal and service account keys are identity-backed: they stop working when the user leaves the organization or the service account is archived. Anthropic recommends them over legacy workspace keys.

Never ship keys to browsers. Call the API from your back end; direct browser calls need the `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true` header and are blocked entirely for ZDR or Compliance API organizations.
Alternatives to static keys: Workload Identity Federation (short-lived tokens exchanged from your IdP at `POST /v1/oauth/token`) and App Attest for iOS/macOS apps.

example.title: SDK picks up the key from the environment
example.code:
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-...   # never commit this
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2026-10-21" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

examTips: Shared CI or production service: service account key (or WIF), not a personal key that breaks when its owner leaves.
Best way to eliminate static secrets in cloud/CI workloads: Workload Identity Federation.
A key in browser JavaScript is always the wrong answer; proxy through a back end.

sections.heading: Workspaces and workspace selection
notes: Every organization has an undeletable, unrenamable **Default Workspace**. Extra workspaces (IDs start with `wrkspc_`, default cap of 100 per organization) separate projects, environments, or teams under shared billing.
Each workspace can have its own members, service accounts, keys, rate limits, and monthly spend limits. Rate limits are set under Rate limits in the Console; spend limits on the Workspaces page.

A key scoped to one workspace only works there and the request can omit the workspace ID. A key not scoped to a workspace must send the `anthropic-workspace-id` header, otherwise the API returns 400 `invalid_request_error`.
Unknown workspace or no access returns 404 `not_found_error`. The response header `anthropic-workspace-id` tells you which workspace a request ran in.
Workspace roles are per-member (for example workspace developer, limited developer, billing). The workspace billing role cannot be assigned manually; it is inherited from the org billing role.
The Claude Code workspace separates Claude Code traffic and is the only workspace supporting per-user monthly spend limits.

example.title: Select a workspace for an unscoped key
example.code:
from anthropic import Anthropic
client = Anthropic(default_headers={"anthropic-workspace-id": "wrkspc_01JwQvzr7rXLA5AGx3HKfFUJ"})
msg = client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=256,
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}])

examTips: Environment isolation (dev vs prod, team spend caps) is a workspace job.
Missing workspace header with an unscoped key gives 400, not 401.

sections.heading: Organizations and Console roles
notes: Five organization-level roles: **user** (playground), **claude_code_user** (playground and Claude Code), **developer** (playground and manage API keys), **billing** (playground and billing details), **admin** (all of those plus manage users).
Owners and primary owners have all admin permissions and can also manage admins.
When inviting people for Claude Code via the Console, the **Claude Code** role lets them create only Claude Code API keys; the **Developer** role lets them create any API key.
Invites can be bulk-sent from the Members page, or provisioned with SSO.
The Admin API is not available for individual accounts; you need an organization set up in the Console.

example.title: Update a member role via the Admin API

examTips: Least privilege for engineers who only use Claude Code: claude_code_user (or the Claude Code invite role).
Only admin-level roles can manage users or provision Admin API keys.

sections.heading: Admin API and Admin API keys
notes: The Admin API manages members, invites, workspaces, and API keys programmatically (endpoints under `/v1/organizations/...`).
An **Admin API key** starts with `sk-ant-admin...`, goes in the `x-api-key` header, and only organization members with the admin role can provision one.
Alternative credentials: an OAuth bearer token with the `org:admin` scope, or a personal/service account key that is not scoped to a workspace.
Service account, federation issuer, and federation rule endpoints accept only an `org:admin` OAuth token, not an Admin API key.
An Admin API key is for administration, not inference; keep it separate from normal model-calling keys and out of application code.
Enterprise (claude.ai) organizations use a scoped key created in claude.ai; analytics reading needs the `read:analytics` scope.

example.title: List workspaces with an Admin API key

examTips: Prefix to remember: `sk-ant-admin` (admin) vs `sk-ant-api` (regular).
Creating a service account programmatically needs an org:admin OAuth token.

sections.heading: Key expiration, rotation, and leaks
notes: Choose an expiration at creation: presets of 3 hours, 1 day, 7 days, or 30 days, a custom duration, or Never. An org maximum-expiration policy can remove Never. Expiration cannot be changed later.
Expired keys return 401 `authentication_error` and cannot be reactivated; create a new key.
Anthropic emails the creator 7 days before expiry for keys with at least 14 days of lifetime, and 1 day before for keys with at least 7 days.
Disable is reversible (status `inactive`, then Re-enable); Delete is permanent (status `archived`).
The Admin API reports `expires_at` (null for no expiry) so you can audit keys before they lapse.
Rotation pattern: create the new key, deploy it to the secrets manager or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, confirm requests succeed, then delete the old key.
Extra controls: store keys in a secrets manager, and turn on IP allowlisting to limit where a leaked key works.

example.title: Zero-downtime rotation steps
example.code:
1. Create new key (scoped to the integration's workspace, with expiration)
2. Update secrets manager / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the deployment
3. Verify requests succeed with the new key
4. Delete (not just disable) the old key
5. If a key leaked: Disable immediately, then Delete after replacing

examTips: Suspected leak: disable or delete immediately; expiration alone is not a substitute for hygiene.
Never rotate by deleting first; deploy the new key, verify, then delete the old one.

sections.heading: Claude Code authentication methods and precedence
notes: Account options: Claude Pro/Max/Ultra subscription, Claude for Teams/Enterprise, Claude Console (API billing), cloud providers (Bedrock, Vertex/Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry), and a Claude apps gateway.

Precedence when several credentials exist: (1) cloud provider vars `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`_VERTEX`/`_FOUNDRY`; (2) `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer); (3) `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (X-Api-Key); (4) `apiKeyHelper` output; (5) `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; (6) Anthropic profile/federation credentials; (7) subscription OAuth from `/login`.
In interactive mode you are asked once to approve a custom `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; in `-p` mode the key is always used when present.
A stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` overrides a subscription once approved and can cause failures if its org is disabled. Fix with `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; check `/status`.

Credential storage: macOS Keychain (fallback `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode 0600); Linux `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode 0600; Windows under `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates them and enables multiple accounts.
The Console sign-in has a keyless OAuth option (recommended) or the legacy create-an-API-key option.
Cloud sessions always use subscription credentials and ignore `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

example.title: Diagnose which credential is active
example.code:
env | grep -E 'ANTHROPIC_(API_KEY|AUTH_TOKEN)|CLAUDE_CODE_(USE_|OAUTH_TOKEN)'
unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY   # fall back to subscription login
claude
# inside the session:
/status                   # shows the active credential and org

examTips: Memorize the order: cloud provider > AUTH_TOKEN > API_KEY > apiKeyHelper > OAUTH_TOKEN > profiles > /login subscription.
Subscription user hits an unexpected billing or auth error: look for a leftover ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

sections.heading: apiKeyHelper, setup-token, and OAuth tokens
notes: `apiKeyHelper` is a settings key naming a shell script that prints an API credential; use it for dynamic or rotating secrets such as short-lived tokens from a vault.
`CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` sets the interval for refreshing helper credentials. A helper slower than 10 seconds triggers a warning; failures surface as 'Your apiKeyHelper script is failing'.
`claude setup-token` runs the browser flow and prints a one-year OAuth token. It does not store it; you export it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for CI and scripts.
That token needs a Pro/Max/Ultra/Team/Enterprise plan, can only make model requests (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors), and locally configured MCP servers still work.
Bare mode (`--bare`) does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` there.
`apiKeyHelper`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` apply to the CLI and surfaces wrapping it (VS Code, Agent SDK, GitHub Actions) but not Desktop or cloud sessions.

example.title: apiKeyHelper fetching from a vault

examTips: CI without a browser: `claude setup-token` then CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription) or an API key.
Rotating or vault-issued short-lived creds: apiKeyHelper.

sections.heading: Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and enterprise SSO
notes: Cloud provider mode is selected by environment variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`) or the 3rd-party platform option in the login wizard; no browser login to Anthropic is needed.
Auth then flows through the cloud's own IAM; settings such as `awsAuthRefresh`, `awsCredentialExport`, and `gcpAuthRefresh` supply refreshed cloud credentials.
Teams adds SSO, billing management, and server-managed settings; Enterprise adds domain capture, role-based permissions, and the compliance API. Console organizations can also use SSO.
Admins restrict logins with `forceLoginMethod` (`claudeai`, `console`, or `gateway`) and `forceLoginOrgUUID` in managed settings; `allowedProviders` limits which services a machine may reach.
With `forceLoginOrgUUID` or `forceLoginMethod` set, sessions using `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` are blocked at startup, since org membership cannot be verified.
Deploy login-restricting keys through MDM or managed files, because server-managed settings arrive only after a user authenticates.

example.title: Managed settings pinning login and providers

examTips: Force employees onto the company org: forceLoginMethod plus forceLoginOrgUUID in managed settings.
Cloud-provider vars outrank everything else in Claude Code's credential precedence.

sections.heading: MCP server authorization (OAuth)
notes: Remote HTTP MCP servers authenticate with OAuth: run `/mcp` in Claude Code and finish the browser login. Tokens are stored securely and refreshed automatically; use Clear authentication in `/mcp` to revoke.
Shell equivalents: `claude mcp login <name>` and `claude mcp logout <name>`.
`claude -p` and Agent SDK runs cannot open the OAuth flow; authenticate from an interactive session first.

For servers without Dynamic Client Registration, pre-register: `--client-id`, `--client-secret`, and `--callback-port` (matching `http://localhost:PORT/callback`). In CI set `MCP_CLIENT_SECRET` to skip the masked prompt.
The `oauth` config object supports `clientId`, `callbackPort`, `authServerMetadataUrl` (https override of discovery), and `scopes` (a space-separated string that pins scopes).

A static `Authorization` header is treated as the credential and disables OAuth fallback for that server. `headersHelper` is a command printing JSON headers, run fresh per connection (10 s limit), re-run on 401/403.
Client secrets live in the system keychain or a credentials file, not in config, and can only be set at add time.
examTips: Adding an Authorization header to an OAuth server stops OAuth from being used.
Headless pipelines cannot do interactive OAuth; use headers/headersHelper or sign in beforehand.

sections.heading: Secrets in MCP config: env expansion and scopes
notes: `.mcp.json` supports `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expansion in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, and `headers`. The default applies only when the variable is unset (empty counts as set).
An unset variable with no default stays unexpanded and produces a warning in `claude mcp list` and `/mcp`.

Credential variables (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `HTTPS_PROXY`) expand to empty in a remote server's `url` and `headers`, so a repo cannot exfiltrate them. Copy the value to a variable with your own name to pass it.

Scopes: local (default, `~/.claude.json`, private), project (`.mcp.json`, committed and shared), user (`~/.claude.json`, all projects). Precedence: local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai connector, whole-entry, no merging.
Commit `.mcp.json` with `${VAR}` references only, never literal tokens.
Interactive sessions prompt before using project-scoped servers; a cloned repo cannot approve its own servers.
examTips: Shared secret-bearing server config: commit .mcp.json with ${VAR}, put the value in each developer's environment.
`${VAR:-default}` is the answer when a missing variable should not break the config.

sections.heading: Deny rules for secret files and the sandbox boundary
notes: Block file tools from secrets with `permissions.deny`, for example `Read(./.env)`, `Read(./.env.*)`, `Read(./secrets/**)`. Matching files are also excluded from discovery and search, and Edit/Write are blocked on those paths.
Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow; the first match wins. An allow rule cannot carve an exception out of a deny.
Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not the model, so CLAUDE.md instructions do not replace them. A `.claudeignore` file has no effect.

Read/Edit deny rules cover built-in file tools, recognized Bash file commands (`cat`, `head`, `sed`, `tee`) and redirections. They do **not** cover a script that opens files itself or `grep -r` without naming the file.
For OS-level enforcement against all processes, enable the **sandbox**. Bash patterns like `Bash(curl *)` are not a security boundary either; they miss `/usr/bin/curl` or `sh -c`.
Put org-wide denies in managed settings, where they cannot be overridden; `deny` and `ask` rules apply immediately even in untrusted project settings.
examTips: Deny beats allow always; specificity does not matter.
Need to stop a Python script from reading .env? Deny rules are not enough; use the sandbox.
Instructions in CLAUDE.md are guidance, not enforcement.

sections.heading: Settings precedence and where credentials live
notes: Settings precedence, highest first: managed, command line (`--settings`), project local (`.claude/settings.local.json`), shared project (`.claude/settings.json`), user (`~/.claude/settings.json`).
List keys such as `permissions.allow` merge across files rather than override.
`.claude/settings.local.json` is for personal, uncommitted values; Claude Code adds it to global git excludes when it writes it, but add it to `.gitignore` yourself if you created it by hand.
The `env` block sets variables for sessions and subprocesses; do not put real secrets in committed `.claude/settings.json`.
A telemetry export variable in `env` is ignored from project/local settings, and `permissions.defaultMode` `auto`/`bypassPermissions` do not take effect from them either.
Some restrictive keys (for example `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories: true`) are honored from any scope even over managed settings.

example.title: Keep a personal key helper out of git
example.code:
# project .claude/settings.json (committed): deny rules only
# ~/.claude/settings.json (user): apiKeyHelper path
# .claude/settings.local.json: personal overrides, gitignored
echo '.claude/settings.local.json' >> .gitignore

examTips: A managed deny cannot be overridden by user, project, or --settings.
Secrets belong in user-scope settings, a secrets manager, or env vars, never committed project files.

sections.heading: Gateway patterns (LLM gateway and Claude apps gateway)
notes: A gateway keeps the provider key server-side; developers hold per-developer gateway credentials, giving attribution, budgets, audit logging, and one-credential offboarding.

Point Claude Code at an LLM gateway with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and supply a gateway credential via `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer) or `apiKeyHelper`. Setting only the base URL leaves a saved claude.ai login as the active credential.
While a gateway credential or apiKeyHelper is active, requests use it instead of the subscription login and are billed per token to the credential owner.
Rollout: deploy the gateway with the provider credential, issue per-developer credentials, distribute base URL and credential via managed settings and secrets tooling, then verify on each machine.
To lock a machine to a gateway, set `allowedProviders: ["customEndpoint"]` and pin `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in the managed `env` block (v2.1.285+).

The self-hosted **Claude apps gateway** signs developers in with corporate SSO via `/login`, issues a gateway token that is the session's only credential, and routes inference to Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, or Foundry. It outranks provider variables.
Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through a gateway, and the gateway must forward features Claude Code needs (such as the OAuth `anthropic-beta` capability).

example.title: Developer environment for an LLM gateway
example.code:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://llm-gateway.corp.example.com
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=$(vault read -field=token secret/dev/$USER)
claude
/status   # confirm the credential in use

examTips: Per-developer attribution and central key custody: gateway with per-developer credentials.
Gateway needing Bearer auth: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; needing rotating creds: apiKeyHelper.
SSO sign-in with inference through your own cloud: Claude apps gateway.

keyTakeaways: Regular API keys start `sk-ant-api...`; Admin API keys start `sk-ant-admin...` and only admins can create them.
Prefer personal keys for your own work, service account keys or Workload Identity Federation for shared and automated workloads; workspace keys are legacy.
Keys not scoped to a workspace must send `anthropic-workspace-id`; omitting it gives 400.
Key expiry presets: 3 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, custom, or Never; it cannot be changed later; expired keys return 401.
Rotate by creating, deploying, verifying, then deleting the old key; Disable is reversible, Delete is permanent.
Console roles: user, claude_code_user, developer, billing, admin (owners/primary owners above).
Claude Code credential precedence: cloud provider vars, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, profiles, subscription /login.
`claude setup-token` yields a one-year `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for CI; it is subscription-only and not read in bare mode.
MCP OAuth: authenticate with `/mcp`; a static Authorization header disables OAuth for that server; `-p` runs cannot do the flow.
`.mcp.json` supports `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}`; commit references, not secrets; credential vars read as empty in remote url/headers.
Deny rules are evaluated deny, ask, allow with first match winning; they do not stop arbitrary subprocesses, so use the sandbox for OS-level enforcement.
Gateways keep provider keys server-side; use ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper.

glossary.definition: Static secret from the Console used as a bearer token or x-api-key to call the Claude API.
Key that manages org members, invites, workspaces, and keys; provisioned only by admins.
Organizational unit (wrkspc_ ID) with its own keys, members, rate limits, and spend limits.
Non-human identity that owns keys or federation rules for shared and automated workloads.
Exchanges an IdP identity token for a short-lived Claude API token, removing static keys.
Claude Code setting naming a script whose output is the API credential, for rotating secrets.
One-year subscription OAuth token from claude setup-token, for CI and scripts.
Env var sent as Authorization: Bearer, typically for LLM gateways.
Managed setting restricting claude.ai logins to specified organization IDs.
MCP config command that prints JSON auth headers, run fresh on each connection.
permissions.deny entry such as Read(./.env); checked before ask and allow.
OS-level enforcement that restricts file and network access for all processes, unlike permission rules.
Proxy between Claude Code and a provider that holds provider keys and centralizes usage, cost, and audit.
Self-hosted gateway giving SSO sign-in and routing to Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS.

quiz.q: A production microservice calls the Claude API and the engineer who created its personal API key is leaving. What should the admin do to avoid an outage?
options: Keep the personal key; it keeps working after removal
Create a service account, issue it a key (or use WIF) scoped to the workspace, deploy it, then delete the old key
Create a legacy workspace key and share it by email
Move the key into browser code
quiz.explanation: Personal keys are archived when the user leaves the org. Shared workloads should use a service account key or WIF. Workspace keys are legacy; browser code exposes secrets.

quiz.q: A request using an API key that is not scoped to a workspace returns 400 invalid_request_error. What is the fix?
options: Send the anthropic-workspace-id header or use a workspace-scoped key
quiz.explanation: Unscoped keys must specify the workspace via the header; scoped keys can omit it. It is not an auth failure so rotation or header swaps do not help.

quiz.q: Which credential can provision and manage workspaces and members through the Admin API?
options: sk-ant-api key from the developer role
sk-ant-admin key created by an org admin
quiz.explanation: Admin API keys start with sk-ant-admin and only admins can create them. A workspace-scoped personal/service key is not accepted by the Admin API, and the setup-token only makes model requests.

quiz.q: You need to programmatically create a service account and federation rule. Which credential works?
options: A personal key scoped to one workspace
quiz.explanation: Service-account, federation-issuer, and federation-rule endpoints accept only an org:admin OAuth token.

quiz.q: A contractor should be able to use Claude Code billed through the Console but must not manage keys or users. Which Console role fits best?
quiz.explanation: claude_code_user covers the playground and Claude Code. Developer manages keys, admin manages users, billing manages billing.

quiz.q: A key was created with a 7-day expiration and the team needs 30 days. What can you do?
options: Edit the expiration in the Console
Create a new key with the desired expiration
Use the Admin API to extend expires_at
quiz.explanation: Expiration is set at creation and cannot be changed; expired keys cannot be reactivated.

quiz.q: A developer with a Claude Max subscription suddenly sees authentication failures in Claude Code after joining a new team. env shows ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set to a key from a disabled org. What is happening and the fix?
options: Subscription credentials outrank API keys; reinstall
The approved ANTHROPIC_API_KEY outranks the /login subscription; unset it and check /status
quiz.explanation: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ranks above subscription OAuth once approved. Unset it to fall back to the subscription.

quiz.q: Both ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 are set. Which does Claude Code use?
options: Bedrock, since cloud provider variables rank first
quiz.explanation: Precedence starts with cloud provider variables, then AUTH_TOKEN, API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, OAUTH_TOKEN, profiles, /login.

quiz.q: A CI runner has no browser. The team has a Claude Team subscription and wants to run Claude Code there. What is the right approach?
options: claude setup-token locally, then set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the runner
quiz.explanation: setup-token prints a one-year token for CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Bare mode does not read it, so --bare needs an API key or apiKeyHelper.

quiz.q: Your company issues short-lived Claude credentials from a vault every hour. How should Claude Code obtain them?
quiz.explanation: apiKeyHelper is designed for dynamic or rotating credentials, with the TTL variable controlling refresh.

quiz.q: An admin wants all developers to log in only with accounts in the company's claude.ai org. Where and how?
options: Managed settings via MDM: forceLoginMethod claudeai plus forceLoginOrgUUID
Server-managed settings only, before first login
quiz.explanation: These keys must be deployed through managed/device management, since server-managed settings arrive only after authentication. CLAUDE.md is not enforcement.

quiz.q: A team commits .mcp.json for an internal HTTP MCP server that needs a bearer token. What is the secure pattern?
options: Use "Authorization": "Bearer ${INTERNAL_API_TOKEN}" and set the variable in each developer's environment
Name the variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY so it is trusted
quiz.explanation: Commit ${VAR} references only. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other credential variables read as empty in remote url/headers by design.

quiz.q: An MCP server supports OAuth, but an engineer adds a static Authorization header to its config. What results?
options: Claude Code uses the header as the credential and does not fall back to OAuth
quiz.explanation: A static Authorization header becomes the credential and disables OAuth fallback for that server.

quiz.q: A pipeline runs `claude -p` against an OAuth-protected MCP server and fails to authenticate. Why?
options: -p and SDK runs cannot open the OAuth flow; sign in interactively first or use headers
Project servers are never loaded in -p
quiz.explanation: The documented behavior is that OAuth cannot be initiated in -p or Agent SDK runs.

quiz.q: You add Read(./.env) to permissions.deny and an allow rule Read(./.env) in user settings. A Python tool Claude runs opens .env directly. What is true?
options: Allow wins since it is more specific
Deny wins for Claude's file tools, but the Python subprocess is not covered; enable the sandbox for OS-level enforcement
quiz.explanation: Evaluation is deny, ask, allow with first match; specificity does not change it. Deny rules do not cover arbitrary subprocess reads, so the sandbox is needed.

quiz.q: An org wants one place for audit logging, per-developer budgets, and no provider keys on laptops. Which design fits?
options: Give each developer the org Console API key
Run an LLM gateway holding the provider key; issue per-developer credentials and distribute ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus a credential via managed settings
Share a setup-token across the team
quiz.explanation: Gateways keep provider keys server-side and give per-developer attribution, budgets, and audit.

quiz.q: A developer sets only ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the company gateway but is still billed on their subscription. Why?
options: Without a gateway credential variable or apiKeyHelper, the saved claude.ai login remains the active credential
quiz.explanation: Setting only the base URL does not replace the subscription credential; add ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper.
